name: Green Brown
lede: Green Brown is a plain descriptive name for a dull olive-khaki; as a swatch it is RAL 8000, a paint standard, and the books say little about it as a color.

sections.title: A name that describes itself
sections.body:
Green Brown is the name of RAL 8000, one of the colors in the German RAL paint standard, and this screen value is approximate [1]. A second well-known list, the xkcd color survey, uses the same two words for a much darker, olive-green value, so the name alone does not fix the color [1].

No book in our shelf traces the name to a person, a pigment or a place. Its origin is undocumented, and it is a compound of two basic words, [[green]] and [[brown]] [1].

sections.title: Where the books say green-brown
sections.body:
Books do use the words, mostly for materials. The Pigment Compendium describes several minerals as green-brown, among them diopside, which is typically green but may also be green-brown, and amphiboles such as actinolite [2]. Alkali feldspars can be green-brown in some metamorphic rocks, and the lead tungstate stolzite forms crystals in a range that includes green-brown [2].

In Finlay's *Colour*, the words describe something less pleasant: the dark, crumbly, impure gamboge that a Hong Kong dealer kept from the war years, nothing like the clean pigment [3]. In every case the term is plain description, with no history of its own.

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: The swatch has a lightness of about 49 and a chroma of about 29, which makes it a muted mid-tone [1]. The nearest named color in the archive is [[sepia]], 8.5 units away, a loose match [1]. We found no archive count for this exact swatch, so none is claimed.

disambiguation.gloss: a green-yellow olive; Green Brown is browner and duller
